turns.user: Which section of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 sets out when a perpetual injunction may be granted?

gold.answer: Section 54 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 provides that a perpetual injunction may be granted to prevent the breach of an obligation existing in favour of the applicant.

evidence.quote: a perpetual injunction may be granted to prevent the breach of an obligation existing in favour of the applicant

turns.user: Under the Contract Act, 1872, who is competent to enter into a contract?

gold.answer: Under section 11 of the Contract Act, 1872, every person who has reached the age of majority under the law to which he is subject, is of sound mind, and is not disqualified from contracting by any law is competent to contract.

evidence.quote: Every person is competent to contract who is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, and who is of sound mind, and is not disqualified from contracting by any law to which he is subject.

turns.user: In 2024 my father, of his own free will, gave me his house as a gift without taking any money, and I accepted it. He is still alive.
We live in Hyderabad.
My elder brother is not happy about it.
I have kept all the papers in a safe place.
Going back to what I said first, which section of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 gives the legal definition of what my father did?

gold.answer: Section 122 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 defines a gift: a voluntary transfer of existing property without consideration, accepted by the donee.

evidence.quote: the transfer of certain existing moveable or immoveable property made voluntarily and without consideration, by one person, called the donor, to another, called the donee, and accepted by or on behalf of the donee

turns.user: In 2023 I gave a continuing guarantee to a wholesaler for all the goods my brother buys from him on credit.
My brother runs a small shop in Sukkur.
I work as a schoolteacher.
I am meeting a lawyer next week.
I want to send the wholesaler a notice now. Based on what I told you first, which section of the Contract Act, 1872 lets me revoke it?

gold.answer: Section 130 of the Contract Act, 1872: a continuing guarantee may be revoked by the surety at any time, as to future transactions, by notice to the creditor.

evidence.quote: A continuing guarantee may at any time be revoked by the surety, as to future transactions, by notice to the creditor.
